articles.author: Loading Blocks
articles.description:
1. Block Time, Not Real Time



In Solidity, block.timestamp gives the timestamp of the block that included your transaction, ** not the exact submission time**
All transactions in the same block share the same block.timestamp

This means "first come, first served" logic cannot rely on precise timestamps.
The old keyword now was just an alias for block.timestamp, but it's deprecated now. 
block.timestamp returns a Unix timestamp, i.e., the number of seconds since January 1, 1970(Uinx epoch)

It's a standard across computer science, not unique to Solidity.
Solidity provides time units: seconds,minutes, hours, days, weeks.
These can be used directly in expressions:


block.timestamp + 1 days
block.timestamp - 7 days
This improves readablity and prevents errors from using "magic numbers".
You can implement expiry logic by setting a deadline in the constructor:





uint public expiry;

constructor() {
    expiry = block.timestamp + 1 minutes;
}

function addOne() public {
    require(block.timestamp < expiry, "Contract has expired");
    count++;
}


This pattern enables time-based features like token vesting, limited auctions, or timed voting.
Correct time handling = safer and more predictable smart contracts.
Four pillars:
Block time consensus model.
Unix timestamp standard.
Readable time units in Solidity
Lifecycle enforcement via expiry checks.
articles.title: Time Handling

articles.author: Moss ux
articles.description:
Intro


UX design is more than colors and layouts — it’s the difference between a product people love and one they leave. A smooth experience means higher trust, better engagement, and more conversions. For startups, SaaS, and even small businesses, good design is a growth tool, not an afterthought.
1. First Impressions Decide Everything
When users land on your product, they judge it in seconds. A clean interface with clear navigation feels reliable. A messy layout feels risky, and users bounce.
2. UX = Higher Conversions
Design directly affects whether people sign up, buy, or leave. Every extra click adds friction.
👉 Quick wins:
Shorten forms (ask only what’s necessary).
Add feedback (loading states, success messages).
Use progress steps in onboarding.
These small design choices keep users moving forward instead of dropping out.
3. Design Builds Your Brand
Consistency in color, typography, and layout builds recognition. When everything feels unified, users trust the brand behind the product.
👉 Example: A SaaS dashboard with the same design system across web and mobile instantly feels professional.
Wrap Up
Design isn’t decoration — it’s strategy. From first impressions to conversions to branding, UI/UX shapes the way people see and use your product.
If you’re working on SaaS or startup projects and want design that’s clean, modern, and built for growth, check out Designfy.me.
articles.title: Good Design Isn’t Just Pretty — It Converts
